cards: Father Otto Meyer finds the first recorded Lapita sherds on Watom Island, off New Britain
Edward Gifford and Richard Shutler excavate the site of Lapita in New Caledonia
The Lapita cemetery at Teouma on Efate, Vanuatu, is discovered
James Cook watches the ʻinasi first-fruits ceremony at Muʻa
Tāufaʻāhau defeats Laufilitonga at the Battle of Velata
Laufilitonga, the last Tuʻi Tonga, dies and the title lapses
Nan Madol becomes a UNESCO World Heritage Site and is listed as in danger
Jacob Roggeveen reaches the island on Easter Sunday, 5 April
James Cook finds that some moai have already been toppled
The missionary Eugène Eyraud arrives and later first reports the rongorongo tablets
Atamu Tekena and eleven chiefs sign an agreement with Chile’s Policarpo Toro
William Bligh’s HMS Bounty arrives at Matavai Bay to collect breadfruit plants
Tu’s son, the future Pōmare II, is invested with the red-feathered maro ‘ura
London Missionary Society missionaries land from the Duff at Matavai Bay
Pōmare II defeats the chiefs of the old religion at the Battle of Fei Pi
Pōmare II issues Tahiti’s first written law code and is baptised
Pōmare IV signs a request for French protection under threat of bombardment
Pōmare V cedes Tahiti and its dependencies to France
Kamehameha I wins the Battle of Nuʻuanu and takes Oʻahu
Kaumualiʻi of Kauaʻi accepts Kamehameha as overlord, completing unification
The kapu system is abolished after the death of Kamehameha I
Kamehameha III grants the kingdom’s first constitution
Britain and France jointly recognise Hawaiian independence
The Great Māhele divides the kingdom’s land
Kalākaua is forced to sign the Bayonet Constitution
Queen Liliʻuokalani is overthrown and a Provisional Government proclaimed
Tāufaʻāhau defeats Laufilitonga at the Battle of Velata on Lifuka
Tāufaʻāhau becomes Tuʻi Kanokupolu and King George Tupou I
The fall of Pea and Houma ends the civil wars on Tongatapu
George Tupou I’s code frees commoners from forced service to chiefs
The constitution makes Tonga a constitutional monarchy
A Treaty of Friendship makes Tonga a British protected state
Tonga regains full independence and joins the Commonwealth
Reforms give the people a majority of elected seats in parliament
Six colonies federate as the Commonwealth of Australia on 1 January
Women gain the right to vote and stand in federal elections
Australian and New Zealand troops land at Gallipoli on 25 April
Singapore falls and Japanese aircraft bomb Darwin
The ANZUS Treaty allies Australia with the United States
A referendum allows Aboriginal people to be counted in the census
The Australia Act ends the remaining legal links with Britain
The High Court’s Mabo decision recognises native title
Parliament adopts the Statute of Westminster, completing legislative independence
ANZUS Treaty signed with Australia and the United States; Legislative Council abolished
Britain joins the EEC, ending New Zealand's secure British market
Treaty of Waitangi Act creates the Waitangi Tribunal
French agents sink the Rainbow Warrior in Auckland harbour
Nuclear Free Zone Act passed; te reo Māori becomes an official language
First election under mixed-member proportional representation
Christchurch mosque shootings; most semi-automatic weapons banned
